questions.text: A high-hazard Group G paint storage room is directly below a Group B office suite. If the designer uses a fire-resistance separation rather than relying only on automatic protection, what minimum fire-resistance rating is source-backed for the hazardous storage condition?

options.text: 1-hour
2-hour
3-hour
4-hour

questions.rationale: RA 9514 Section 10.2.6.10(A) supports at least four-hour fire resistance for storage hazards greater than normal occupancy; high-hazard cases may require both construction and automatic protection.

questions.text: An architect is revising a mixed-use building design to correct fire-safety deficiencies. The current plan shows: (1) Group D storage separated from Group B office by a 1.5-hour wall, (2) a central exit stairwell with 1.5-hour wall rating, and (3) a Group G chemical storage room separated from adjacent Group B space by a 2-hour wall. How many of these three separations are non-compliant with Philippine codes?

options.text: Zero—all three are compliant, meeting the minimum fire-resistance requirements
One separation is non-compliant, requiring additional fireproofing measures
Two separations are non-compliant, necessitating a redesign of the fire safety plan
All three separations are non-compliant.

questions.rationale: All three fail minimum requirements: (1) Group D requires 2-hours; (2) Multi-story exit stairs require 2-hours; (3) Group G requires 4-hours. [A]: All fail to meet the minimum standards of PD 1096 and RA 9514. [B]: More than one is incorrect. [C]: All three are deficient. [D]: Correct. 1.5-hour is too low for Storage and Stairs (2hr), and 2-hour is too low for Group G (4hr).
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 Rule VII Table VII.4, RA 9514 IRR Rule 10

questions.text: Which statement is source-safe when evaluating whether a wall or floor is fire-rated?

options.text: A material name alone proves the hourly rating
Untaped gypsum board automatically satisfies any two-hour requirement
A fire rating is unnecessary if the finish schedule lists noncombustible materials
The required rating must be tied to the code condition and a verified rated assembly or tested/listed construction

questions.rationale: The repaired article keeps source-backed code conditions and avoids unsupported material shortcuts.

questions.text: Under RA 9514 Section 10.2.5.2(B), what fire-resistance rating is required for a protected exit that connects three storeys or less?

options.text: At least 1-hour
At least 2-hour
At least 3-hour
At least 4-hour

questions.rationale: RA 9514 distinguishes protected exits connecting three storeys or less from those connecting four or more storeys.

questions.text: Under RA 9514 Section 10.2.5.2(B), what fire-resistance rating is required for a protected exit separation when the exit connects four or more storeys?

options.text: 20 minutes
45 minutes
1-hour
2-hour

questions.rationale: A protected exit connecting four or more storeys requires at least two-hour fire resistance.
questions.code_citation: RA 9514 IRR Rule 10, PD 1096 Rule VII

questions.text: A paint storage room has a hazard greater than normal office occupancy. Which source-backed protection path should the architect check first?

options.text: Treat it as Group D storage and use a 2-hour rule
Use ordinary corridor rules
Apply the RA 9514 special-hazard rule: at least four-hour fire resistance, automatic fire protection, or both; high hazard requires both
Use parking-structure geometry rules

questions.rationale: RA 9514 Section 10.2.6.10(A) controls hazards greater than normal occupancy.

questions.text: A high-rise office building has a central required exit stair. Which design is source-backed as incorrect under the protected-exit rule?

options.text: A protected exit separation with at least 2-hour fire resistance
A protected exit enclosure serving many storeys with only 1-hour fire resistance
Openings protected by approved self-closing fire-resistive doors
Noncombustible construction supporting the protected exit separation

questions.rationale: For exits connecting four or more storeys, RA 9514 requires at least two-hour fire resistance.

questions.text: A question describes a "Group D storage" room beside a Group B office. What is the first source-backed correction?

options.text: Answer 2-hour because all storage is Group D
Answer 1-hour because it is an office building
Flag the premise: PD 1096 Group D is Institutional; storage/hazardous uses belong under Group G or the special-hazard rule
Use PD 1096 Rule XIX

questions.rationale: PD 1096 Group D is Institutional, not Storage. Storage and hazardous uses are Group G.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 Rule VII Table VII.4, RA 9514 IRR Rule 10

questions.text: A required central exit stair connects four or more storeys, but the architect specifies only 1-hour protected-exit separation. Is this compliant under RA 9514?

options.text: Yes, because 1-hour is enough for all protected exits
Yes, if the building is an office
No, four or more storeys require at least 2-hour fire resistance
No, all protected exits require 4-hour separation

questions.rationale: RA 9514 Section 10.2.5.2(B) requires at least two-hour fire resistance where a protected exit connects four or more storeys.

questions.text: A laboratory contains a Group G high-hazard paint storage room beside a Group B office. What source-backed protection should the architect coordinate?

options.text: No separation because both rooms are in one building
1-hour ordinary corridor separation
2-hour Group D storage separation
At least four-hour fire resistance, automatic fire protection, or both; high-hazard use requires both

questions.rationale: RA 9514 special-hazard provisions apply to storage hazards greater than normal occupancy; high-hazard uses require both rated construction and automatic protection.
